properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (second pass, same day): after the shear fix above, a user-flagged visual check still showed this block overlapping paved streets. Root cause found: several blocks (PKN, PKS, HDY3, HDY1/2, E4) had their OWN corner pixel positions misread during transcription -- e.g. PKN's west edge was recorded as pixel x=163 when the diagram's own gridline labels put it at x=355 (which is where the Illinois St anchor point itself was measured). This was a transcription slip, not a transform error -- the 6-point transform's anchors were unaffected (confirmed: A, B, C1, C2, D, E1, E2, E3, F/G, H1, H2 were read correctly the first time). Re-read all 5 affected blocks' corners directly against their crop images' own labeled gridlines and recomputed. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (fifth pass): user-flagged check found this block's boundary itself (not a clipping artifact) was missing an entire row of real, currently-used parking near 20th St -- the diagram-derived north edge sat ~25m south of the lot's actual northern extent. Measured directly against satellite imagery (same method as the west-edge fixes on B/E1/E2) and moved the north edge to the real curb/crosswalk line at 20th St. CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-09-14 (seventh pass): user clarified the diagonal row of angled cars along this block's west side is curbside parking on Illinois Street itself, not part of the PKN/PKS parcel -- the earlier fixes had mistakenly extended the west edge to include it. Pulled the west edge back east to -122.3874, matching where the diagonal on-street parking row ends and the lot's own perpendicular-grid parking begins (visually distinct in the satellite image). CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (eighth pass): auditing this block for the same curb-vs-lot-line mistake found and fixed on Pier 70 Building 2 (see that file's digitization_method, failure mode 6 in src/bearing_trace.py), a user-flagged review found the north edge (set in the fifth pass above) still had exactly that bug -- it was anchored on the 20th St curb/crosswalk line, one row of real angled parking too far north. That front row runs at a different angle than the rest of the lot's parking, has no visible separation from the street/crosswalk itself (i.e. it reads as curbside street parking, not a lot with its own frontage), and is set off from the second (and subsequent) rows by a real gap with a visible pavement-color change -- the same 'significant white separation' signal already used to exclude curbside parking on this block's west edge. Re-anchored the north edge at that second-row transition (approx. lon -122.38695, lat 37.76041) using this site's established grid bearing and line_intersection(). This moved the north edge roughly 7-8m south of the fifth-pass version. THIS WAS WRONG, CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (ninth pass): user clarified the eighth pass misread the imagery -- the diagonal row immediately south of the street IS part of PKN's own lot (it shares the same angle and spacing as the rest of the lot's parking), not curbside street parking. What actually sits between the street and that row is a much thinner sliver -- a single line of vehicles parked facing a DIFFERENT direction (parallel to the curb, not angled into the lot) -- that thin sliver, not the whole first diagonal row, is the real on-street parking to exclude, and it has no visible delimitation from the street itself (matching the earlier west-edge lesson: on-street parking reads as part of the street, not the lot). Re-measured the true boundary at the top edge of the diagonal row (where the angled spaces actually begin, immediately past that thin curbside sliver and the street's own paved width): lon -122.38696, lat 37.76061 -- essentially the SAME position as the fifth-pass version (within ~1m), confirming the fifth pass had already found the right line and the eighth pass's 'fix' was a real regression, not a correction. Lesson generalized in src/bearing_trace.py: when applying the curbside-parking-exclusion pattern, check the EXCLUDED band's own vehicle orientation and depth before assuming a whole matching row is street parking -- a thin, differently-angled sliver right at the curb is the real signal, not simply 'the row closest to the street.' STILL WRONG, CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (tenth pass): the ninth-pass fix anchored the whole north edge on a SINGLE measured point (at the west end) plus the site's established perpendicular bearing (86.5 degrees), rather than this specific edge's own two-point bearing -- exactly the shortcut this project's own bearing_trace.py methodology warns against (derive an edge's bearing from that edge's own two endpoints, not a borrowed one), and it produced a line that hugged the real row's top edge correctly at the west end but drifted north into the gap above the row by the east end. User annotated two separate crops (west portion and east end near the building corner) showing the true row-top edge; extracted the marked line's actual pixel path in both images and converted to real coordinates (rather than eyeballing), giving two well-separated points -- (-122.38702427, 37.76055681) and (-122.38675117, 37.76056792) -- 24m apart. Their own bearing (87.06 degrees) is close to the established 86.5 (confirms the site bearing was never the problem) but using these two real points directly, rather than one point plus an assumed bearing, fixed the drift: the resulting edge now hugs the row's top consistently at both ends, confirmed by zooming into each end separately after the fix. STILL WRONG, CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (eleventh pass): user pointed out the tenth-pass line still cut through a visible sidewalk -- a clearly lighter, more uniform-toned paved band sitting between the excluded curbside sliver and the real diagonal parking, distinct in color/texture from the lot's own darker, worn pavement. Confirmed quantitatively: averaging pixel brightness in bands parallel to the tenth-pass line (canceling out individual-car noise) showed a bright, ~3.5m-deep band immediately south of that line before brightness dropped off into the lot's own darker pavement -- i.e. the tenth-pass line sat inside the sidewalk, not at its far edge. Moved the edge 3.65m further south (same bearing, both endpoints shifted equally) to the point where the bright band ends and the lot's own pavement begins. Overlay-confirmed at both ends: a clearly lighter band is now visible between the old and new lines, and the new line sits right at the top of the real parking row with no sidewalk-toned pavement above it. TWELFTH PASS, same day (west/east edges): user asked to apply the same color-based criteria to the west and east edges, which had not been re-audited since their much earlier fixes. West edge: found the committed line ran straight through a second, distinct column of diagonal parking, splitting it in half -- there is a real walkway/gap west of that column (between it and the truly-curbside first column along Illinois St), and the whole second column sits on the PKN side of that walkway. Moved the west edge (both NW and SW, same bearing, parallel shift) 5.27m further west to that walkway, confirmed by zooming into both a wide view and a close-up: the previously-split column is now fully included and the true curbside-only column stays excluded. East edge: initially over-corrected by expanding 5.5m east, based on a large open paved apron that had similar color/texture to the lot -- user caught this: a curving driveway edge visible at the south end of that same apron indicates it's a road/driveway curve, not more lot, despite the matching pavement color. Reverted the east edge (NE, SE) back to its prior, un-expanded position -- ground color alone was not sufficient here without also reading the shape of the boundary (a curving edge is a strong road/driveway signal that overrides a same-color match). REVERTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 border-alignment audit): the twelve satellite-imagery-driven passes above were built on a mistaken premise -- this project maps the D4D's PLANNED layout (including streets and open space not yet built) against today's satellite imagery as a backdrop, not the other way around. Snapping this parcel's boundary to today's real parking-lot striping was wrong: it silently deleted 'Public Open Space' shown directly on Figure 6.4.2 (a green strip between this block and 20th St) and erased '21ST ST (NEW)' entirely, a real, deliberately-labeled future street the diagram draws with its own paved width between PKN and PKS. Re-traced this block directly from Figure 6.4.2 instead: programmatic pixel-color detection (isolating this legend color, RGB [169,143,173]) found this block's own purple fill spans pixel x 420-665, y 475-787 in the 2376x1836 source image (y=475 is where the fill begins, south of the green open-space strip; y=787 is this block's south edge, north of 21ST ST (NEW)'s own ~35px/~20m-wide drawn width) -- converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform used for this site's other numbered parcels. This restores the diagram's own street and open-space gaps that the satellite-snapping passes had collapsed to zero. The satellite-based lessons above (curbside-parking exclusion, sidewalk-color detection, driveway-curve reading) remain useful technique notes for tracing REAL/existing features elsewhere in this project, but do not apply to this PLANNED parcel's own boundary. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (streets/block-alignment review, prompted by a user request to audit street alignment sitewide): the pixel measurement immediately above ('x 420-665, y 475-787') was taken from a 2376x1836-resolution copy of Figure 6.4.2, but was then run through this site's 6-point affine transform, which was calibrated against the 2200x1700-resolution page171.png -- a resolution mismatch that silently shifted this whole block by the 2376/2200 = 1.08x scale factor (the same class of bug independently found and fixed on Building 21's old trace). Re-measured directly on page171.png (2200x1700) with the same color-isolation method: this block's true purple fill is pixel (389,440)-(578,728), a clean rectangle -- notably narrower on the east side than the old (665, unscaled) reading, which turns out to have also simply misread that edge (verified: a pixel scan at y=600 shows the fill ending at x~578-580, then a black border, then white street pavement -- there is no fill out to x=615 (665/1.08), so the east edge was doubly wrong, not just unscaled). Cross-checked against the neighboring blocks this touches: the corrected PKN-PKS gap (21st St NEW) is now 15.4m (previously reported as 19-26m under the old, larger trace -- both are plausible street widths, but 15.4m is what the corrected geometry actually gives), and this fix also required correcting the '20th Street Plaza' frontage strip (data/manual/pier70_pkn_frontage_plaza.geojson), which had explicitly copied this block's old (wrong) x-range and south-edge y-value -- see that file's own digitization_method. CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-09-17 (same day, after PKS was found badly mispositioned): PKS was ground-truthed against the real 21st St centerline and moved ~25m south (see pier70_pks.geojson) -- as a direct consequence, this block's own south edge, while not itself overlapping any real street (only 4.5% buffer overlap, not flagged), left an oversized ~40m gap to PKS's new position, far wider than Figure 6.4.2's own drawn '21ST ST (NEW)' width (~20m) or this street's real curb-to-curb width (~13-15m, measured elsewhere in this project). Extended this block's own south edge further south to close that gap: interpolated the real 21st St centerline's latitude at this edge's own two longitudes and set the edge 6.8m north of it (the same real curb-to-centerline half-width used sitewide). New PKN-PKS gap is 13.5m, consistent with the street's real measured width; confirmed 0 overlap with 21st St itself. RE-INVESTIGATED 2026-09-17 (yet again, same day, after user feedback called the prior revert-and-redo cycle 'mostly a downgrade' and asked for a clarifying question rather than another guess): went back to first principles instead of more pixel geometry. Two checks, both requested by the user: (1) searched the D4D's own text (Section 4.11, Specific Streets Design Intent) for any description of 21st St being relocated or realigned -- found none; it describes 21st St as 'primarily serves as an alley from Illinois Street to the waterfront,' with no mention of a moved alignment. (2) Pulled real satellite imagery (src/satellite_check.py) directly over where DataSF's official centerline (CNN 15232000/15233000) says 21st St runs between Illinois and Michigan St -- it shows vegetation, graded dirt, a tree, and a vehicle-storage yard: zero pavement. So the earlier 'the D4D relocates 21st St' theory (this file's own prior REVERTED/RETRACTED entries) was an overreach from a real but simpler fact: DataSF's centerline here is a paper (platted, unbuilt) alignment, the same failure mode as three other already-excluded CNNs in street_geometry.py (12915000, 15200000, 15228000) -- not a deliberate relocation. Added CNN 15232000/15233000 to that same exclusion list, with the satellite evidence documented there. User's explicit instruction: note that this stretch of 21st St isn't built yet, but for this map's purpose (showing the planned FUTURE parcel state) treat the diagram's own drawn '21ST ST (NEW)' position as authoritative. Restored this block to its pure diagram-transform position accordingly -- the same value already found and confirmed multiple times this project (most recently before the mistaken ground-truth shift below). REPOSITIONED 2026-09-17 (user override: 'take my input as override... turn that Michigan span into 21st st and adjust parcel positioning accordingly'): re-anchored to the corrected planned 21st St line (see pier70_21st_street.geojson -- built from Michigan St's own real terminus point, perpendicular to Illinois/Louisiana's real ~175.5-degree bearing), replacing the Figure 6.4.2 pixel-traced position used previously. Only this block's south edge changes (north/east/west edges, anchored to real 20th St, are untouched): snapped to the new anchor line's position 6.8m north of its centerline (this project's curb half-width) at each corner's own longitude. This block grows -- its south edge moves further south than the previous pixel-traced position, since the new, real-anchored '21st St (NEW)' sits further south than the diagram pixel trace did. ADJUSTED 2026-09-17 (two user-flagged issues, same pass): (1) east edge extended to real Michigan St (this block's previous east edge stopped well short of Michigan St's real position, leaving an unclaimed ~13-19m gap the user called out as 'arbitrary') -- computed Michigan's real centerline (CNN 8999001) at this block's own corner latitudes and set the edge 9.8m west of it (6.8m curb + ~3m sidewalk allowance, per the D4D's own cited 55-67ft ROW range for this class of street). (2) north edge moved south by 10m ('a notch,' a judgment call per the user's own phrasing, not a diagram or survey measurement) to give the 20th St Plaza more depth, since this block's own south edge had already grown substantially in the prior round -- see pier70_pkn_frontage_plaza.geojson for the matching extension. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: 'HDY3 should border Illinois like PKS and PKN, in the continuity'): this block's own SW corner, PKS's NW/SW corners, and HDY3's NW corner had each been independently traced/measured against Illinois St at different times, leaving a several-meter 'wobble' between the three blocks' own west edges instead of one continuous line. Recomputed this block's SW corner from a single shared formula (used identically on PKS and HDY3): interpolate real Illinois St's centerline (CNN 7169000) longitude at this corner's own latitude, then offset 9.8m east (this project's standard curb+sidewalk allowance) -- see pier70_hdy3.geojson's own digitization_method for the full writeup covering all three blocks together.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). RE-TRACED 2026-09-17 directly from Figure 6.4.2 at the correct source resolution (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. This deliberately does NOT match today's satellite imagery of the parking lot -- this parcel's boundary represents the D4D's planned footprint, including '21ST ST (NEW)' and the '20th Street Plaza' open-space strip (data/manual/pier70_pkn_frontage_plaza.geojson), neither of which is built yet.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
properties.regulatory_context: Residential, 65 ft max / 6 stories, 245 for-sale condominium units, 377,506 sf building, Handel Architects. Developer is TMG Partners + Presidio Bay Ventures -- NOT Brookfield; this parcel was purchased directly from the Port in Feb 2019 and is 'fully entitled' but has no confirmed groundbreaking as of the most recent research pass (2026).
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat.
